stem: When managing a child with suspected bowel obstruction, why is it recommended to start antibiotics?

options.text: To treat the viral infection that likely caused the obstruction
To prevent sepsis from transmigration of organisms through the compromised bowel wall
To reduce the size of the hypertrophied pyloric muscle
To stimulate the return of normal bowel peristalsis
To relieve abdominal pain by reducing bowel spasm

explanation: Preventing sepsis is the reason antibiotics are started in bowel obstruction, because pressure and compromised blood supply can allow organisms to translocate across the bowel wall.
rationale: Compromised bowel integrity can permit bacterial translocation and subsequent sepsis.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because bowel obstruction is usually a mechanical or surgical problem, and antibiotics do not treat viral causes.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because pressure and reduced perfusion in an obstructed bowel can compromise the bowel wall, allowing bacterial translocation and sepsis.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because antibiotics do not reduce pyloric muscle hypertrophy.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because antibiotics do not restore bowel motility or act as prokinetic agents.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because antibiotics are not primary analgesics for bowel spasm.

source.hint: Think about what happens to bacteria when the intestinal barrier is under pressure or lacks blood flow.
